title: ROI heuristics and scenarios sketch for private deployments
content:
Executive summary:

This sketch collects a set of heuristics and concrete scenario drafts to help the Product and Solutions teams evaluate near-term ROI for Private deployments (on-prem vs VPC) and to recommend licensing + support bundle configurations. The objective is practical: create a small, reproducible scenario matrix we can hand to Sales and Solutions Engineering to produce ballpark quotes and identify which customers will materially benefit from a Private purchase vs continued Hosted usage.

Key takeaways (high level):
- For customers with sustained baseline throughput > 6M tokens/day and predictable 24/7 workloads, dedicated on-prem hardware often breaks even inside 18–30 months if they accept standard 3yr amortization for GPUs and a modest ops headcount.
- VPC (cloud-hosted private control plane + cloud GPU instances) favors mid-size customers (1.5M–6M tokens/day) because it avoids heavy up-front capex while still offering isolation and network controls.
- Licensing should be tiered by committed tokens/day and include two core components: platform license (flat monthly per-cluster) + per-token service fee (to cover KV cache, model updates, RLHF syncs). Support tiers should map to SLA targets and required runbooks (S1/S2 vs S3).

Scope and audience:
This doc is a working draft for: Product, Solutions Engineering, Pricing, and Sales engineers. It's intentionally lightweight; the next step is to translate these scenarios into a small spreadsheet with the following tabs: assumptions, scenarios, annualized cost curves, break-even timelines, recommendation engine.

Approach and main assumptions (defaults used across scenarios):
- Model mix: 70% generation (gpt-like open model), 30% embeddings/batch tasks.
- Average token length (user + assistant): 120 tokens per request.
- QPS profile: peak-to-baseline multiplier = 3x for bursty workloads.
- Target utilization for on-prem GPUs: 60% steady-state (accounting for maintenance, headroom, model warmup).
- Hardware pricing (list price, non-binding): A100-equivalent node (4x GPUs) = $360k capex per cluster; amortized over 3 years with 0% salvage. Networking & racks (on-prem) = $40k initial.
- Cloud VPC instance pricing: $/GPU-hour assumed at $3.25 (sustained discounted price for reserved monthly VPC instances).
- Personnel: 0.15 FTE per 1M tokens/day for day-to-day ops; escalation SRE/infra retained by Redwood for managed private control plane is priced separately.
- Licensing: base license = $12k/month/cluster; per-1M-tokens/day commitment discount tiers apply.
- Support tiers: Standard (included) with 48h response; Premium (+25% license) with 4h response and guaranteed escalation rota; Enterprise (+50% license) with named support lead and quarterly onsite.

Scenario definitions (three canonical scenarios):
1) Small steady consumer SaaS (S): 0.8M tokens/day baseline, moderate bursts to 2.4M. Goal: VPC private control plane for compliance.
2) Mid-market product (M): 3.2M tokens/day baseline, bursts to 9M. Goal: evaluate VPC vs small dedicated on-prem cluster.
3) Large enterprise (L): 12M tokens/day baseline, sustained 24/7 throughput. Goal: on-prem cluster(s) with dedicated ops and premium support.

Worked-through sketch calculations (rounded):
- On-prem capital amortization: for a 4x GPU cluster at $360k + $40k infra = $400k total. Amortized per year over 3 years = $133k/year. With 60% utilization and our token model, estimate tokens/year served (generation-weighted): for L (12M tokens/day) -> 4.38B tokens/year. Cost basis per-1B tokens/year = $133k / 4.38 = ~$30k.
- Personnel (ops): assume one 0.6 FTE SRE plus 0.2 FTE infra engineer for on-prem L clusters -> blended fully-loaded cost $220k/year. Per-1B tokens this maps to ~$50k.
- Licensing/support: enterprise license + premium support equals ~ $200k/year fixed. Per-1B tokens ~ $45k.
- Cloud VPC at mid-range (M): 3.2M tokens/day -> ~1.17B tokens/year. If per-GPU-hour cloud cost for matching throughput is $3.25 and effective GPU-hours/year for that token load ~ 1,200 hours per GPU * n GPUs chosen, the quick conversion yields cloud spend ~ $360k–$450k/yr depending on sustained usage/discounts. Add platform license $144k/year (12k*12) and lower ops (0.3 FTE) -> blended cost sits around $600k/yr. Per-1B tokens ~ $500k.

Interpreting the numbers (heuristic):
- On-prem large clusters move the per-token fixed-cost envelope down significantly (order-of-magnitude lower per-1B tokens) but require high utilization and longer payback windows.
- VPC is operationally simpler for mid-size customers and provides cost predictability; the delta vs Hosted API often narrows when customers commit to 12+ months and reserve capacity.

Licensing + support bundle recommendations (draft):
- Base bundle (Starter): $12k/month cluster license, Standard support included. Target: customers < ~1M tokens/day or low security needs but want private control plane.
- Growth bundle: $28k/month cluster license, includes 1yr reserved VPC capacity discount, 8x5 support. Recommended for 1–6M tokens/day customers.
- Enterprise bundle: $55k/month cluster license, premium support, onboarding package, optional on-site quarterly review. Recommended for >6M tokens/day and on-prem engagements.
- Add-ons: SLO-backed latency SLAs, extended retention for observability logs, HSM/KMS integration. Price per add-on should be presented as percentage uplift to license (e.g., HSM +20%).

Optimization levers to emphasize in proposals (these reduce effective TCO):
- Model consolidation: moving from several model families to 1–2 core variants reduces GPU memory fragmentation and allows denser packing -> expect 12–22% effective cost improvement.
- Quantized weights + integer kernels: conservative estimate 18–30% GPU-hour savings for generation workloads with negligible quality loss for many use-cases.
- Prefix/KV caching for conversational workflows: 10–25% token cost reduction; highlight as a configuration savings we can manage centrally.
- Autoscaling policies + burst-backing to Redwood hosted (hybrid): capex reduction with cloud-bursting for predictable peaks. Useful for mid-market customers uncertain about steady-state.

Checklist for Sales/SE for quick quotes (template algorithm):
1) Gather baseline tokens/day (7-day average) and peak multiplier.
2) Ask about model family(s) and required latency percentile.
3) Estimate utilization and map to cluster count using tables in the spreadsheet (we'll prepare).
4) Apply recommended license band and suggested support tier; present both VPC and on-prem numbers side-by-side with break-even timeline and 3-yr NPV using a default discount rate.
5) Include optimization levers as separate line items with expected delta and confidence scores (High/Medium/Low).

Decision heuristics for recommending VPC vs on-prem: (simple rule-of-thumb)
- Recommend VPC when baseline < 2M tokens/day OR customer explicitly wants minimal on-site ops or shorter payback (<24 months).
- Recommend on-prem when baseline > 8M tokens/day and the customer can commit to 2+ year amortization horizon, or when strict data residency and zero-tenant rules exist.
- For 2–8M tokens/day, present both with a hybrid option and emphasize usage volatility: high volatility -> VPC, low volatility -> on-prem.

Open questions and follow-ups (to turn this sketch into the formal spreadsheet):
- Validate accurate GPU-hour -> tokens conversions across model families (ask Applied ML to produce a 3-point estimate per model).
- Confirm discount schedules for 12/24/36 month reserved VPC capacity with Cloud Partnerships.
- Formalize personnel fully-loaded rate cards by region (we used US-blended rates in this sketch).
- Map SLO uplift percentages to support bundle pricing more rigorously (engagement with SRE/pricing required).

Next steps and timeline:
- Week 1: Seed a small spreadsheet using these assumptions and add tabs for each scenario + a sensitivity heatmap (Aisha / Miguel).
- Week 2: Get Applied ML baseline conversions and update GPU-hour rules (Samira).
- Week 3: Run 15 representative customer profiles through the sheet to validate break-even thresholds (Solutions Eng / Sales).
- Week 4: Incorporate cloud discount confirmations and produce two templated customer decks (one for VPC-first, one for On-prem-first).

Appendix: quick note on NPV example (3-yr):
- Using a 10% discount rate, a $400k up-front on-prem investment with annual opex of $180k and license $200k/year yields payback in ~22 months in the L scenario; NPV over 3 years is positive if baseline usage assumptions hold.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally a rough, persuasive sketch not a polished billing model. Avoid sharing externally until we turn it into the canonical spreadsheet and get Applied ML validation.
- If you have specific customer cases (Jira or spreadsheet export) drop them in the linked artifacts list and we'll run them through the matrix.

-- end of sketch --
